title: A New, Rapid Method for the Quantification of Dolichyl Phosphates in Cell Cultures Using TMSD Methylation Combined with LC–MS Analysis

For the preparation of liquid chromatography, mobile phase A (Solvent A) and mobile phase B (Solvent B), and wash solvents, please see Recipes. Solutions 15 M KOH (see Recipes) 10 M AmAc (see Recipes) Solvent A: acetonitrile/water 60:40 (v/v) with 0.1 % FA and 10 mM AmAc (see Recipes) Solvent B: isopropanol/water 90:10 (v/v) with 0.1 % FA and 10 mM AmAc (see Recipes) Wash solvent: dichloromethane:methanol:water (3:48:47, v/v/v) (see Recipes) Dichloromethane:methanol mixture (6.5:5.2, v:v) (see Recipes) 155 mM ammonium bicarbonate buffer (see Recipes) Recipes 15 M KOH Accurately weigh 8.4 g of KOH pellets into a 100 mL volumetric flask. Add LC-grade water dropwise with intermittent slow vortex to dissolve KOH. Be careful, as an exothermic reaction will occur, and the reaction flask will be hot. After complete dissolution, dilute the solution to the mark. Use a glass bottle with a PTFE lid for storage of the KOH solution. 10 M AmAc Take the 10 mL volumetric flask along the glass stopper and rinse both twice with MS-grade methanol. Dry them carefully under Argon. Transfer accurately weighed 7.708 g of LC-MS grade AmAc to the volumetric flask. To dissolve the solid, add distilled water in steps of approximately 100 µL, followed by sonication. Once all solids are dissolved, fill the volumetric flask to the etched line. This stock can be stored at 4 °C for up to six months. Solvent A: acetonitrile/water 60:40 (v/v) with 0.1 % FA and 10 mM AmAc Prepare 1,000 mL of solvent mixture of acetonitrile/water 60:40 (v/v) and add 1 mL of formic acid and 1 mL of 10 mM AmAc stock. Mix solvent mixture thoroughly and degas for 5 min in an ultrasonic water bath sonicator. Solvent B: isopropanol/water 90:10 (v/v) with 0.1 % FA and 10 mM AmAc Prepare 1,000 mL of solvent mixture of isopropanol/water 90:10 (v/v) and add 1 mL of FA and 1 mL of 10 mM AmAc stock. Mix solvent mixture thoroughly and degas for 5 min in an ultrasonic water bath sonicator. Wash solvent: dichloromethane:methanol:water (3:48:47, v/v/v) Dichloromethane:methanol mixture (6.5:5.2, v:v) 155 mM ammonium biocarbonate buffer Transfer accurately weighed 1.2 g of ammonium bicarbonate into a 100 mL volumetric flask. Dissolve in distilled water and make up to the mark with distilled water. This stock can be stored at 4 °C for up to six months.

steps.title: Prepare stock solutions and reagents
steps.instruction: Prepare all required stock solutions according to the Recipes: 15 M KOH (dissolve 8.4 g KOH pellets in water, dilute to 100 mL, store in PTFE‑capped glass bottle); 10 M ammonium acetate (weigh 7.708 g, dissolve in water with sonication, dilute to 10 mL, store at 4 °C up to 6 months); Solvent A (1 L acetonitrile/water 60:40 v/v, add 1 mL formic acid and 1 mL 10 mM ammonium acetate stock, mix, degas 10 min in ultrasonic bath); Solvent B (1 L isopropanol/water 90:10 v/v, add 1 mL formic acid and 1 mL 10 mM ammonium acetate stock, mix, degas 10 min); Wash solvent (dichloromethane:methanol:water 3:48:47 v/v/v); Dichloromethane:methanol mixture (6.5:5.2 v/v); 155 mM ammonium bicarbonate buffer (dissolve 1.2 g in water, dilute to 100 mL, store at 4 °C up to 6 months).

steps.title: Thaw samples and perform initial extraction
steps.instruction: Work on ice or in a cold room. Thaw HeLa/fibroblast or S. cerevisiae cell pellets on ice for 20 min (skip for HeLa extraction). Suspend yeast pellets in 200 µL 155 mM ammonium bicarbonate buffer, add 0.5 mm glass beads, vortex 1 min, then centrifuge 3 500 × g 1 min at room temperature (RT). Transfer the aqueous top layer to a clean microcentrifuge tube, add 20 pmol internal standard PolP C60, add 1 mL methanol, vortex 1 min and sonicate 1 min, then add 1 mL water, vortex 1 min and sonicate 1 min, and centrifuge 3 500 × g 5 min at RT. (Optional) Measure total lipid or phosphatidylcholine levels now if normalization is desired.

steps.title: Alkaline hydrolysis and phase partitioning
steps.instruction: Use round‑bottom screw‑top glass tubes with Teflon caps. Fill a water bath with distilled water to the level of 2.5 mL solvent in the immersed tube and heat to 85 °C. Add 0.5 mL 15 M KOH to each sample, vortex 1 min, centrifuge 3 500 × g 5 min at RT, then place tubes in the 85 °C water bath with linear shaking at 40 rpm for 1 h. Cool to RT, vortex 1 min, centrifuge 3 500 × g 5 min at RT. Raise water level in the bath to the level of 7.5 mL solvent, heat to 40 °C. Add 1 mL methanol and 4 mL dichloromethane to each tube, vortex, then incubate at 40 °C with shaking at 40 rpm for 1 h. Cool to RT, vortex, centrifuge 3 500 × g 5 min at RT. Remove the upper aqueous phase with a Pasteur pipette, wash the lower organic phase four times with the wash solvent, and transfer the organic phase to a new glass tube. Dry the organic extracts under a gentle stream of nitrogen at RT using a Turbovap evaporator.

steps.title: Methylate dolichyl phosphates (including QC)
steps.instruction: In a screw‑top glass tube, combine 20 pmol DolP standard and 20 pmol internal standard, dry under nitrogen. Add 200 µL dichloromethane:methanol mixture (6.5:5.2 v/v), vortex 1 min, centrifuge 3 500 × g 5 min at RT. Add 10 µL trimethylsilyldiazomethane (TMSD) using a gas‑tight Hamilton syringe, vortex 1 min, centrifuge 3 500 × g 5 min at RT, and incubate 40 min at RT. If the yellow color of TMSD disappears, add TMSD in 5 µL increments until a faint yellow persists. Quench excess TMSD by adding 10 µL acetic acid (add in 5 µL increments until the yellow color disappears). Dry the methylated samples under nitrogen at RT in the Turbovap.

steps.title: Reconstitute samples for LC‑MS analysis
steps.instruction: Reconstitute each dried sample in 120 µL methanol, vortex 1 min, transfer the solution to a Neochrom micro insert placed in a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube, centrifuge 1 500 × g 5 min at 4 °C, and then place the micro insert into an LC vial for analysis.

steps.title: Prepare LC system and gradient
steps.instruction: Place solvents A and B on the LC system, purge all lines for 5 min, set flow rate to 0.1 mL/min with a 60:40 (A:B) ratio, and maintain the column at 55 °C. Equilibrate the column for at least 15 min after pressure stabilizes. Program the gradient: 0 min 40 % B, 0–3 min 40 %→50 % B, 3–9 min 50 %→54 % B, 9–9.1 min 54 %→70 % B, 9.1–17 min 70 %→90 % B, 17–27.5 min 90 % B, 27.5–27.6 min 90 %→40 % B, 27.6–30 min 40 % B.

steps.title: Configure MS parameters and inject samples
steps.instruction: Calibrate the Q‑Exactive Plus mass spectrometer (positive ESI mode) with XCalibur. Set: spray voltage 3.5 kV; scan range 960–1600 m/z; sheath gas 30 L/min; auxiliary gas 10 L/min; spare gas 1; collision energy NCE 50 %; S‑Lens 50 eV; maximum ion trap time 100 ms; resolution AGC target 17 500 at m/z 200; MS1 target 2 × 10⁵; MS2 target 7 × 10⁴ at m/z 200; MS2 target 3 × 10⁶; capillary temperature 250 °C. Inject 100 µL of each sample in the following order: run a solvent blank at least three times for gradient stabilization, inject a QC sample to verify methylation and system performance, then inject the randomized study samples.

description: Validation of protocol The method mentioned in the present protocol has been thoroughly validated according to ICH guidelines [see supplementary information mentioned in Kale et al. (2023)]. The following method validation parameters were tested: lower limit of quantification (LOD) and the linearity range, intra- and inter-day accuracy and precision, extraction recovery, and post-preparative autosampler stability. As described in Kale et al. (2023), the analytical procedure provided acceptable values of validation parameters tested, and the experimental protocol was robust and reproducible.
